pages.text: Last one. The writing's shaky, so I'll be brief, which Marnie will tell you is a first.$(br2)If you're reading this warm, in the dark half of the year, with somebody's kid asleep by the fire, then it worked, and it wasn't me.
pages.title: Entry Five

pages.text: I only ever got this valley to hold on. You got it to stay.$(br2)Everything I know, somebody taught me on a bad afternoon with better things to be doing. My mother taught me the porch trick. Bram's father taught me to read a wheel.

A woman whose name I have genuinely forgotten taught me to bank an oven so it holds overnight, in ninety seconds, in the rain, because I looked cold.$(br2)None of them saw what I did with it. That's normal. That's the arrangement.

Wheel goes counter-clockwise. Third lamp post leans, always has. Marnie takes her tea far too strong.$(br2)Don't turn this into a monument. Don't put my name on the square. Put a bell there, and ring it when supper's ready.

Somebody will come up the road next spring. They do, when there's smoke. Go and meet them. Bring bread. Pretend you were passing.$(br2)-- J.K.$(br2)$(italic)(P.S. There's a lamp post on my porch with nothing on it. I'd like to be on the line.)$()
